/en-gb/airport-assistance/: Flight delayed, cancelled or bag lost on a UK–Thailand trip? How to report it to the operating airline at the airport, records to keep, Thai CAAT rights and BA proof for Allianz UK claims.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airlines/: UK–Thailand airline help: British Airways from Gatwick, Thai Airways and EVA Air from Heathrow, and Norse Atlantic’s planned Manchester service, with delay certificates and baggage claim steps.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airlines/briti: British Airways Gatwick–Bangkok guide: South Terminal check-in closes 60 minutes before long-haul departures, Bag Drop times by cabin, baggage phone lines and Customer Relations proof for insurers.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airlines/eva-a: EVA Air Heathrow–Bangkok: BR67 and BR68 use Terminal 2, with staffed check-in, tag printing and bag drop times, airport office and baggage numbers, plus delay certificate and baggage claim steps.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airlines/norse: Norse Atlantic Manchester–Bangkok flights are planned from Terminal 2 from 5 December 2026 to 18 April 2027. Covers check-in windows, online check-in rules and the seven-day damaged-bag claim limit.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airlines/thai-: Thai Airways Heathrow–Bangkok nonstops TG910, TG911, TG916 and TG917 use Terminal 2. The London office is closed to visitors, so use phone or email; Bangkok check-in opens eight hours before.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/: Thailand airport guides for UK travellers: choose Bangkok Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, Phuket or Chiang Mai to find terminal facilities, airline check-in desks and onward transport for your flight.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/: Suvarnabhumi Airport guide for first-timers: arrivals, departures and international transfers via Level 3, AOT Limousine on Level 2, the Airport Rail Link on B1, and why Door 4 differs from gate D4.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/m: Suvarnabhumi Airport indoor maps for the main terminal, concourses A–G and the SAT-1 satellite. Search shops, cafés, ATMs, lounges and airline counters by terminal, floor and facility type.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/s: Suvarnabhumi Airport smoking areas: public rooms outside Doors 1 and 10 on Levels 2 and 4, and airside spots reported near Burger King in Concourse D after immigration. Maps by floor included.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/t: Suvarnabhumi Airport to Bangkok: compare the Airport Rail Link from B1, public taxis between Doors 4 and 7 with a 50-baht surcharge plus tolls, Grab from Door 4 on Level 1, and Bolt by hotel area.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/cnx/: Chiang Mai Airport guide: service hours 06:00–24:00, airport shuttle from Door 12 of the international terminal, a 24-hour Grab service centre on domestic Level 1, and a smoking area near Exit 9.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/dmk/: Don Mueang Airport guide: Terminal 1 for international and Terminal 2 for domestic flights, open 24 hours. Floor maps for shops, banks and ATMs, and the smoking area outside Door 8 on Level 3.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/hkt/: Phuket Airport guide: separate international and domestic terminals, international arrivals on Level 1 with belts 1–5, self-check-in on Level 3, Norse Atlantic desks and smoking areas by floor.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/lgw/: London Gatwick to Bangkok: British Airways and Norse Atlantic use the South Terminal. BA long-haul check-in closes 60 minutes before departure; Bag Drop times by cabin and baggage contacts listed.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/lhr/: London Heathrow to Bangkok: Thai Airways and EVA Air check in at Terminal 2. Find EVA’s counter, tag printing and bag drop zones, THAI’s office contact and arrival baggage email.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/airports/man/: Manchester Airport to Bangkok: Norse Atlantic plans a direct winter route from Terminal 2. For arrival baggage problems, use the Excess Baggage Company desk in Terminal 2 or Norse’s baggage email.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/departure-airp: Check-in and contacts at UK airports for Thailand flights: Gatwick, Heathrow and Manchester desks, bag drop, ticket offices and baggage contacts for British Airways, Thai Airways, EVA Air and Norse.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/flights/: Flights between the UK and Thailand: British Airways Gatwick–Bangkok (11 h 50 min), Thai Airways and EVA Air from Heathrow, and Norse Atlantic’s planned Manchester route, with verified dates.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/damaged: Suitcase damaged on a UK–Thailand flight? Show it to baggage staff before leaving, get a PIR, and note British Airways requires damage to be reported within seven days. Keep the bag for assessment.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/eva-dam: EVA Air damaged baggage claims: show the damage to staff at arrival, and claim for damage or partial loss within seven days from the day after collecting your bag, using EVA’s online declaration.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/eva-del: EVA Air delayed or lost baggage: report on arrival, track online with your file reference, and claim within 21 days of the bag’s scheduled arrival. EVA sends an inventory form after five days.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/eva-fli: EVA Air departure and arrival certificate: apply or print online within 180 days of arrival by selecting BR and the flight number, such as 67. Codeshares on other carriers are excluded.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/find-ai: How to find the right airline counter at the airport: check the operating airline, local departure date and flight number, then tell check-in, ticketing and arrivals baggage desks apart.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/insuran: Travel insurance claims for UK travellers: request baggage proof from British Airways Customer Relations, then claim with Allianz UK online or via your bank or broker’s number. Proof is not payment.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/late-ar: Arriving late at Suvarnabhumi after a delay: the Airport Rail Link runs 05:30–24:00, while public taxis between gates 4 and 7 and Grab pickup outside gate 4 on level 1 operate 24 hours.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/norse-d: Norse Atlantic damaged baggage: report on arrival or email baggage@flynorse.com, and claim within seven days of receiving the bag with your PIR. Normal wear and cosmetic damage are excluded.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/thai-da: Thai Airways damaged baggage: take the bag to THAI staff on arrival for a PIR, and register a written claim within seven days. If you have already left, contact your local THAI office promptly.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/thai-de: Thai Airways delayed baggage: report it before leaving arrivals, keep your file reference, and claim expenses in writing within 21 days of delivery. London queries go to the THAI station email.
/en-gb/airport-assistance/guides/thai-fl: Thai Airways disruption certificate for insurance: covers THAI-operated flights arriving over 15 minutes late. Apply from three days to six months after travel with your passport and boarding pass.
/en-gb/attractions/ancient-city-muang-bo: Muang Boran Ancient City in Samut Prakan is an outdoor museum of Thai palace and temple architecture, from the Sanphet Prasat replica to Dusit Maha Prasat. Open daily 09:00–19:00, adults 800 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/aquaria-phuket/: Aquaria Phuket is an indoor aquarium on B1 of Central Phuket Floresta, with otters, penguins, rays and a large marine tank. Open daily 11:00–19:00; buy online tickets at least three hours ahead.
/en-gb/attractions/ayutthaya-historical-: Ayutthaya Historical Park covers the UNESCO-listed ruins of Siam’s old capital: the Buddha head in tree roots at Wat Mahathat, three chedis at Wat Phra Si Sanphet and riverside Wat Chaiwatthanaram.
/en-gb/attractions/bangsaen-aquarium/: Bangsaen Aquarium at Burapha University’s Institute of Marine Science shows tide-pool creatures and coral-reef fish by habitat. Open 09:00–16:00, closed Mondays, with diver feeding daily at 14:30.
/en-gb/attractions/bophut-fishermans-vil: Bophut Fisherman’s Village on Koh Samui’s north coast is a seafront street of old Chinese wooden shophouses turned into shops and restaurants, with hand-carved soap and seafood dinners.
/en-gb/attractions/bridge-over-river-kwa: The Bridge Over the River Kwai in Kanchanaburi is part of the real Thai–Burma Railway built by prisoners of war in 1942–1943. See how it differs from the 1957 film and why trains still use it.
/en-gb/attractions/bueng-boraphet-aquari: Bueng Boraphet Aquarium in Nakhon Sawan has a 24-metre freshwater tunnel and over 33 tanks of freshwater, marine and non-local fish, in its own building within the lakeside visitor complex.
/en-gb/attractions/bueng-chawak-aquarium: Bueng Chawak Aquarium in Suphan Buri splits its exhibits by building: a freshwater tunnel in Building 2, and a marine tunnel with rays, turtles and a shark tank in Building 3. Open from 08:30.
/en-gb/attractions/categories/markets/: Thailand markets guide to 12 night, weekend and floating markets, from Chatuchak and Or Tor Kor in Bangkok to Damnoen Saduak, Amphawa, Chiang Mai’s walking streets and Phuket’s Lard Yai.
/en-gb/attractions/categories/temples/: Temples in Thailand: 30 to visit across Bangkok, Ayutthaya, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Sukhothai and the south, from Wat Pho’s Reclining Buddha to the White Temple and Ayutthaya’s brick ruins.
/en-gb/attractions/categories/theme-wate: Theme parks and water parks in Thailand compared: Siam Amazing Park, Dream World, Andamanda Phuket, Ramayana, Aquaverse and Vana Nava, and why a child ticket does not override ride height limits.
/en-gb/attractions/charoen-krung/: Charoen Krung in Bangkok mixes riverside heritage and creative spaces: TCDC inside the Central Post Office and Warehouse 30, seven wartime warehouses now home to bookshops, a record shop and cafés.
/en-gb/attractions/chatuchak-market/: Chatuchak Market is Bangkok’s big weekend market, open Saturday and Sunday 09:00–18:00. Find fashion in Sections 2–4, vintage in 5–6 and art in 7, reached from MRT Kamphaeng Phet or BTS Mo Chit.
/en-gb/attractions/chiang-mai-night-baza: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar on Chang Khlan Road opens daily from about 16:00 to 23:30 for crafts, clothing and souvenirs. See how it differs from the Wua Lai and Sunday walking streets.
/en-gb/attractions/chiang-mai-night-safa: Chiang Mai Night Safari runs two vehicle routes: Savanna Safari with giraffes and zebras, and Predator Prowl with tigers and lions, plus walking exhibits and shows, separate from Chiang Mai Zoo.
/en-gb/attractions/chiang-mai-zoo/: Chiang Mai Zoo sits at the foot of Doi Suthep, with capybaras, kangaroos, penguins and an aquarium with underwater tunnels. Adults pay 350 baht; the aquarium needs its own ticket.
/en-gb/attractions/damnoen-saduak-floati: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market in Ratchaburi is best in the morning, ideally by 09:00, when fruit and noodle boats ply Khlong Ton Khem. It is about two hours from Bangkok by road.
/en-gb/attractions/erawan-museum/: Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan is crowned by a giant three-headed elephant, with three levels of ceramics, stained glass and Buddha images inside. Open daily 09:00–18:00; adult admission 500 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/jim-thompson-house/: Jim Thompson House Museum in Bangkok is a group of six teak houses beside a canal, seen on a guided tour of the main house. Open daily 10:00–17:00; adults 250 baht, near BTS National Stadium.
/en-gb/attractions/khao-kheow-open-zoo/: Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Si Racha, Chonburi is a large open-range zoo, home to Moo Deng the pygmy hippo, giraffes and white rhinos, with elephant swimming and a penguin parade. Open 08:00–17:00.
/en-gb/attractions/khao-san-road/: Khao San Road is a 300-metre backpacker street in Bangkok’s Old Town with hostels, hotels, travel agents, bars and clubs. Eat anything from pad Thai to falafel; Sam Yot MRT is the nearest station.
/en-gb/attractions/khlong-lat-mayom-floa: Khlong Lat Mayom Floating Market in western Bangkok runs on weekends and public holidays, 08:00–17:00. Eat grilled fish, boat noodles and khanom chin by the canal without needing to board a boat.
/en-gb/attractions/mae-klong-railway-mar: Mae Klong Railway Market in Samut Songkhram is a working market where vendors fold back awnings as the train passes. Trains reach Mae Klong Station at 08:30, 11:10, 14:30 and 17:40; entry is free.
/en-gb/attractions/museum-siam/: Museum Siam in Bangkok explores Thai identity through food, clothing and everyday objects, with hands-on displays. Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00–18:00, admission 100 baht, by Exit 1 of Sanam Chai MRT.
/en-gb/attractions/nakhon-ratchasima-zoo: Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo in Korat is an open-air zoo with African savanna-style exhibits for giraffes, zebras, lions and white rhinos, plus sarus crane conservation. Foreign adults pay 350 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/national-museum-bangk: National Museum Bangkok shows Thai history, Buddhist art and royal funeral chariots in the former Front Palace. Closed Monday, Tuesday and holidays; admission 240 baht, near Tha Chang Pier.
/en-gb/attractions/nimmanhaemin/: Nimmanhaemin in Chiang Mai is a café, gallery and boutique neighbourhood along a 1 km road and its sois, with crafts on Soi 1, the SS1254372 gallery café on Soi 17 and One Nimman nearby.
/en-gb/attractions/nong-khai-aquarium/: Nong Khai Aquarium, also called the Sirindhorn Aquarium, belongs to Khon Kaen University. A 34-metre sloping tunnel leads from marine fish upstairs down to Mekong River species below.
/en-gb/attractions/phuket-aquarium/: Phuket Aquarium at Cape Panwa is a marine research aquarium with an underwater tunnel, touch pool and robotic mermaid. Open 08:30–16:30, with diver feeding in the tunnel tank daily at 11:00.
/en-gb/attractions/phuket-old-town/: Phuket Old Town preserves Sino-Portuguese shophouses from the tin-mining era and Peranakan heritage. Visit Thai Hua Museum on Krabi Road, see street murals and try Hokkien noodles and apong.
/en-gb/attractions/safari-world/: Safari World on the edge of Bangkok pairs a drive-through Safari Park with giraffes, zebras and white rhinos and a walk-through Marine Park with dolphin and stunt shows. Closed on Mondays.
/en-gb/attractions/sea-life-bangkok/: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World is an indoor aquarium in Siam Paragon, with jellyfish and seahorses on B1 and the Ocean Tunnel, Shark Walk and penguins on B2. Open 10:00–20:00; allow 90 minutes.
/en-gb/attractions/taling-chan-floating-: Taling Chan Floating Market in Bangkok has dining rafts on the canal by the district office, open weekends and holidays 07:00–17:00. Eat seafood, boat noodles and som tam, then try krayasat.
/en-gb/attractions/waghor-aquarium/: Waghor Aquarium in King Mongkut’s Science Park, Prachuap Khiri Khan, covers six habitats from rivers and mangroves to coral reefs, with a glass tunnel and specimens. Open 09:00–15:45.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-arun/: Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn on Bangkok’s west bank, has a central prang covered in ceramic fragments, yaksha guardians and hall murals. Open daily 08:00–18:00; foreign visitors pay 200 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-pho/: Wat Pho in Bangkok is home to the 46-metre Reclining Buddha with 108 mother-of-pearl designs on its feet, four royal chedis and traditional massage. Open 08:30–20:00; admission 300 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-phra-kaew/: Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, lies inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace and is included in the 500-baht palace ticket. Look for the Ramakien murals, golden chedis and giant guardians.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-phra-mahathat-nak: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan in Nakhon Si Thammarat is southern Thailand’s great relic temple, centred on a gold-topped chedi ringed by smaller towers, with monks’ quarters to the north and south.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-phra-si-sanphet/: Wat Phra Si Sanphet in Ayutthaya is known for three bell-shaped chedis in a row, each holding the remains of an Ayutthaya king. Walk the hall foundations of this former royal palace temple.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-phra-singh/: Wat Phra Singh in Chiang Mai’s Old City houses the Phra Singh Buddha in Lai Kham Viharn, whose 1860s murals show Lanna stories and dress, beside a golden chedi. Open 07:00–22:00; 50 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-phra-yai-samui/: Big Buddha Koh Samui, Wat Phra Yai, sits on the islet of Koh Fan off the northeast coast. The 12-metre golden seated Buddha dates from 1972 and is reached along a stone causeway built by locals.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-plai-laem/: Wat Plai Laem on Koh Samui gathers a 20-metre white Guanyin, a smiling Phra Sangkatchai figure and temple halls around a pond. Cross the bridges for a closer look, then pair it with the Big Buddha.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-rong-khun/: Wat Rong Khun, Chiang Rai’s White Temple, is a contemporary artwork by Chalermchai Kositpipat, with a white hall, bridge and mythological sculptures. Open 08:00–17:00; admission 200 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-rong-suea-ten/: Wat Rong Suea Ten, Chiang Rai’s Blue Temple, has a vivid blue hall fronted by a great naga, made by a pupil of the White Temple’s artist. Open 07:00–20:00, free to enter, 4 km from the city.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-si-chum-sukhothai: Wat Si Chum in Sukhothai frames the 15-metre Phra Achana seated Buddha behind 3-metre-thick walls and a narrow opening. It lies in the north-west zone outside the walled centre; open 08:30–17:00.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-suthat/: Wat Suthat in Bangkok’s old city stands by the red Giant Swing, with murals, carved wooden doors and the bronze Sisaakayamuni Buddha. Temple 08:30–20:00 for 100 baht; museum on weekends.
/en-gb/attractions/wat-yai-chai-mongkhon: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon in Ayutthaya, founded in 1357, has a great bell-shaped chedi marking King Naresuan’s 1592 victory and a Reclining Buddha by the entrance. Open 08:00–17:00; 40 baht.
/en-gb/attractions/wualai-saturday-marke: Wua Lai Saturday Market in Chiang Mai runs from about 17:00 to 22:00 on the silversmiths’ street south of Chiang Mai Gate, with silver, lacquerware, hill-tribe textiles and street food.
/en-gb/attractions/yaowarat-chinatown/: Yaowarat, Bangkok’s Chinatown, is lined with gold shops, Chinese temples and Chaozhou seafood restaurants. Try steamed fish and crab, then explore Vanich Road’s wholesale lanes.
/en-gb/beaches/chaweng/: Chaweng Beach on Koh Samui’s east coast is a long curve of white sand backed by plenty of hotels. Learn how it differs from Chaweng Noi to the south and what a red flag means for swimming.
/en-gb/beaches/cities/ko-chang/: Koh Chang beaches compared: White Sand Beach (Hat Sai Khao) on the north-west coast for shops and restaurants close by, or Klong Prao further south for a broad, palm-lined walk.
/en-gb/beaches/cities/pattaya/: Pattaya beaches compared: central Pattaya Beach along Beach Road with hotels, restaurants and shops, or Jomtien’s long coast to the south for a quieter walk. Map pins and access notes included.
/en-gb/beaches/cities/phuket/: Phuket beaches compared: lively Patong with restaurants and shops, the long white sand of Karon, and compact Kata on the west coast. See each on the map with road access and swimming notes.
/en-gb/beaches/hua-hin/: Hua Hin Beach runs beside the royal retreat town, ideal for a seaside walk before or after a meal. Check whether horse riding is running and its price, and allow extra time to reach Khao Takiab.
/en-gb/beaches/jomtien/: Jomtien Beach is Pattaya’s long southern shore, lined with hotels and restaurants on the seaside road. Keep clear of water sports equipment, and note that Jomtien Bus Terminal is not by the sand.
/en-gb/beaches/karon/: Karon Beach on Phuket’s west coast is a long stretch of white sand north of Kata, known as Karon Yai. Karon Noi to the north is for hotel guests, and high waves can mean walking rather than swimming.
/en-gb/beaches/kata/: Kata Beach, or Kata Yai, is a compact curved bay on Phuket’s west coast south of Karon, surrounded by hotels, bars and souvenir shops. Kata Noi to the south is a separate beach; avoid surf zones.
/en-gb/beaches/klong-prao/: Klong Prao Beach on Koh Chang’s west coast is a broad, palm-lined stretch south of White Sand Beach. Avoid swimming off the rocky Laem Chai Chet cape, and note some hotels sit back from the road.
/en-gb/beaches/lamai/: Lamai Beach on Koh Samui’s east coast, south of Chaweng, has curved sand and palms. Parts have deep water and strong waves, so keep children close and swim only where permitted that day.
/en-gb/beaches/patong/: Patong Beach on Phuket’s west coast is a lively curved bay backed by hotels, restaurants and shops, reached by road without a boat. Swim away from water sports and follow the lifeguards’ flags.
/en-gb/beaches/wong-duean/: Ao Wong Duean on Koh Samet is a crescent bay of white sand. Take a boat from Ban Phe straight to the bay or land at Na Dan Pier and cross the island; check the landing point when booking.
/en-gb/cameras/chaam-thew-talay/: Cha-am Thew Talay CCTV live cam: still photographs from Thew Talay Estate refresh every few minutes rather than streaming video. Check the capture time to see the sky and landscape before your trip.
/en-gb/cameras/chainat-chao-phraya/: Chai Nat CCTV live cam overlooking the Chao Phraya River and dam area, opened via Webcamera24. A river landscape rather than a beach view; the original operator and stream status are unverified.
/en-gb/cameras/chiangmai-weather-view/: Chiang Mai CCTV live cam directory via EaseWeather: choose from public cameras and refreshed photographs around the city, then read each location name and capture time to check the sky.
/en-gb/cameras/chiangrai-wat-thep/: Chiang Rai Wat Thep Bun Yuen CCTV live cam showing the temple against the surrounding mountains, viewed on Webcamera24. It previews northern scenery but does not show visitor areas or entrances.
/en-gb/cameras/huahin-centara/: Hua Hin Beach CCTV live cam from Centara Grand Beach Resort, showing the coast in front of the hotel and the sea beyond. Play it here or on YouTube, and compare with the KBA kite school view.
/en-gb/cameras/huahin-kba/: Hua Hin KBA CCTV live cam from Kiteboarding Asia, facing the sea, shore and sky off Hua Hin Beach. It shows conditions on camera but does not confirm whether kitesurfing lessons are running.
/en-gb/cameras/krabi-ao-nang-coast/: Krabi Ao Nang CCTV live cam from Thai agency GISTDA, labelled NANG OUT, looking over the sea and sky off Ao Nang. It does not confirm whether boats to Railay or the islands are running.
/en-gb/cameras/lanta-hat-lant/: Koh Lanta CCTV live cam listed as Hat Lant on Webcamera24, showing sea views from the island. The exact beach is unverified, so use it for general scenery rather than a specific stretch of sand.
/en-gb/cameras/nakhon-cha-uat/: Nakhon Si Thammarat Cha-uat River CCTV live cam via Webcamera24, covering riverside scenery in southern Thailand. The exact filming point is unverified and it shows no specific facility or route.
/en-gb/cameras/pathum-chao-phraya/: Pathum Thani CCTV live cam on the Chao Phraya, showing the river and riverside town buildings, found through Tufaq’s camera guide. An inland river view rather than a seaside one.
/en-gb/cameras/pattaya-beach-panorama/: Pattaya Beach CCTV live cam from SkylineWebcams, giving a broad panorama of the shore and the Gulf of Thailand. A wide view of the waterfront rather than close-up waves at the sand.
/en-gb/cameras/phangan-sanskara/: Koh Phangan Haad Rin CCTV live cam from House of Sanskara, looking out over the beach, waves and sky. Watch here or on YouTube; it shows one coast, not conditions across all of Koh Phangan.
/en-gb/cameras/phuket-cape-panwa/: Phuket Cape Panwa CCTV live cam from NĀMA Freediving, looking across NĀMA Bay to the horizon in south-eastern Phuket. Conditions in this quiet bay may differ from the rest of the island.
/en-gb/cameras/phuket-karon-marina/: Phuket Karon Beach CCTV live cam from Marina Phuket Resort, looking along the southern end of Karon’s long white sand towards the sea, waves and sky. Karon lies just north of Kata Beach.
/en-gb/cameras/phuket-kata-surf/: Phuket Kata Beach CCTV live cam: photographs from SSS Phuket refresh periodically to show the sea and incoming waves. Check the capture time, and follow beach flags rather than images before surfing.
/en-gb/cameras/phuket-patong-panorama/: Phuket Patong Bay CCTV live cam showing the town in the foreground, green hills and the sea beyond, a wider view than a beach-only camera. Pair it with the Patong Tower view for the sand.
/en-gb/cameras/samet-cocoon/: Koh Samet CCTV live cam from The Cocoon Hostel, looking from the Na Dan Pier area across the sea towards the mainland. It shows waves and clouds, not ferry departures, so check boat times separately.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-bang-rak/: Koh Samui Bang Rak CCTV live cam from SkylineWebcams, overlooking Bang Rak Beach on the island’s north coast. Use it to tell this beach apart from Lamai or Crystal Bay when choosing where to stay.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-banyan-tree/: Koh Samui Banyan Tree CCTV live cam, filmed from the resort hillside to show the whole bay and beach below. A high viewpoint for the coastline’s shape rather than close-up waves at sand level.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-baobab/: Koh Samui Lamai Beach CCTV live cam from Baobab restaurant, filmed close to the sea to show the sand and incoming waves. A second Lamai view is available from Black Pearl on the same beach.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-black-pearl/: Koh Samui Lamai CCTV live cam in front of Black Pearl, showing waves reaching the shore and the open sea. Watch here or on YouTube, and compare with the Baobab camera further along Lamai Beach.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-bophut-beach/: Koh Samui Bophut Beach CCTV live cam from SkylineWebcams, showing the sand and sea on the island’s north coast. Check the original page for broadcast status; other cams cover Lamai and Choeng Mon.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-choengmon/: Koh Samui Choeng Mon CCTV live cam showing the beach, offshore water and waves on the island’s north-east coast. Useful for telling Choeng Mon apart from Bophut or Bang Rak before you book.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-crystal-bay/: Koh Samui Crystal Bay CCTV live cam from Crystal Bay Yacht Club, showing white sand and waves at Thongtakian Bay. Watch here or on YouTube for a close view of this beach rather than the whole island.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-crystal-beach/: Koh Samui Silver Beach CCTV live cam, listed as the Crystal Bay beachcam by SamuiWebcam on Webcamtaxi, showing the sea and coast near the beach. It is separate from the yacht club camera.
/en-gb/cameras/samui-two-palms/: Koh Samui Bang Po CCTV live cam from Two Palms, showing where the shore meets the sea at Bang Po Beach. Watch on this page or YouTube to picture the seafront near your accommodation.
/en-gb/cameras/tao-island-skyline/: Koh Tao CCTV live cam from SkylineWebcams, looking from a beach across the bay to nearby islands. A combined sea-and-islands view for planning an island holiday; it does not mark beach entrances.
/en-gb/coupons/: Thailand travel deals for UK holidaymakers: this page links to official offers rather than coupon codes, namely GrabFood Thailand on grab.com and the LINE MAN app listing on Google Play.
/en-gb/destinations/: Thailand holiday planning from the UK: entry rules and TDAC for British passports, when to visit Bangkok or the islands, and destination ideas from Chiang Mai and Phuket to Koh Lanta and Koh Samet.
/en-gb/entry/: Thailand entry for British passport holders: visa-free stays of up to 30 days for tourism from 15 September 2026, six months’ passport validity, completing TDAC within three days and arrival steps.
/en-gb/entry/tourist-visa/: Thai tourist visa from the UK: single entry is valid three months for stays of up to 60 days, multiple entry six months. Apply by e-Visa via the London embassy with e-tickets and UK address proof.
/en-gb/entry/visa/: Thai visa types for British passport holders: when the 30-day tourist exemption applies and when you need a tourist, work, study, retirement, DTV or LTR visa via the London embassy’s e-Visa system.
/en-gb/food-delivery/: Food delivery in Thailand compared: GrabFood, LINE MAN, ShopeeFood and Robinhood, with how to order to your hotel, check delivery fees and the final total, and where to collect your order.
/en-gb/food-delivery/grabfood/: GrabFood in Thailand: order through Food in the Grab app, match your hotel address to the map pin, and pay by cash or a foreign credit or debit card. Covers delivery fees, collection and cancelling.
/en-gb/food-delivery/line-man/: LINE MAN food delivery in Thailand: have your LINE ID ready, set your hotel address and map pin, check the total including delivery fees, and contact support through the order if anything is missing.
/en-gb/food-delivery/robinhood/: Robinhood food delivery covers Bangkok and nearby areas. Enter your hotel address to see restaurants that deliver, check the full total, and collect your order where reception tells you.
/en-gb/food-delivery/shopeefood/: ShopeeFood in Thailand is ordered through the ShopeeFood menu in the Thai Shopee app, separate from shopping. Match your hotel address and map pin, then check the final total including delivery.
/en-gb/food/: Food and city views in Thailand: dinner and drinks picks such as Sky Beach and Mahanakhon SkyWalk in Bangkok, HONG’s Sky Bar in Chiang Mai, Baba Nest in Phuket, plus links to food delivery guides.
/en-gb/rooftops/: Thailand rooftop bars and observation decks: compare 44 venues on one map, from Bangkok’s Sky Bar, Sirocco and Mahanakhon SkyWalk to sunset spots in Phuket, Pattaya, Chiang Mai and Koh Samui.
/en-gb/rooftops/abar-rooftop/: ABar Rooftop at Bangkok Marriott Marquis Queen’s Park is an open-air gin and cocktail bar above the city lights on Sukhumvit Soi 22. Open daily 17:00–01:00, casual dress, with reservations by phone.
/en-gb/rooftops/above-eleven/: Above Eleven on the 33rd floor of Fraser Suites Sukhumvit serves Nikkei food, mixing Peruvian and Japanese flavours, with pisco sours, DJ sets and Wednesday salsa nights. Open 17:00–02:00.
/en-gb/rooftops/akara-sky-hanuman/: Akara Sky Hanuman is a Thai mythology-themed sky bar on the 61st floor of One City Centre, Bangkok, open 17:00–02:00. The complex also has an observation deck and night market with their own terms.
/en-gb/rooftops/alfresco-64/: Alfresco 64 is a yacht-styled open-air whisky bar on the 64th floor of lebua at State Tower in Silom, Bangkok, with DJ music and city views. Open 17:00–00:30; smart casual, over-20s only.
/en-gb/rooftops/attic-by-octave/: ATTIC by Octave is a hidden-style bar on the 47th floor of Bangkok Marriott Hotel Sukhumvit, pairing Sukhumvit views with Mexican-inspired drinks and snacks. Smart casual; book via the venue link.
/en-gb/rooftops/baba-nest/: Baba Nest at Sri Panwa, Cape Panwa, is a sunset deck ringed by an infinity pool facing the Andaman Sea. Open 17:00–20:00 by advance booking, with a 3,000-baht minimum spend for non-residents.
/en-gb/rooftops/baiyoke-observatory/: Baiyoke Sky Observatory in Pratunam has a viewing floor on level 77 and a revolving deck on level 84, open daily 10:00–22:00. A good add-on to a Bangkok shopping day; a 450-baht promotion is listed.
/en-gb/rooftops/barbu-pattaya/: BARBÙ on the 24th floor of Siam@Siam Design Hotel Pattaya is a family-friendly rooftop serving Mediterranean sharing dishes with city views, separate from the adults-only Skybar on floor 27.
/en-gb/rooftops/brewski-rooftop/: Brewski Rooftop Bar on floors 29–30 of Radisson Blu Plaza Bangkok serves craft beer and bar food with Sukhumvit views. Open daily 17:00–01:00; arrive early to stay from sunset into the night.
/en-gb/rooftops/char-rooftop/: CHAR Rooftop Bar on the 26th floor of Hotel Indigo Bangkok Wireless Road offers signature cocktails and live music above central Bangkok. It is separate from CHAR Restaurant on floor 25.
/en-gb/rooftops/cities/bangkok/: Bangkok rooftop bars and observation decks: 30 venues mapped, including Sky Bar and Sirocco at lebua, Mahanakhon SkyWalk, Baiyoke Sky and Octave, with booking, admission and directions.
/en-gb/rooftops/cities/pattaya/: Pattaya rooftops and viewpoints: five venues mapped, including Horizon at Hilton Pattaya, Skybar Summer Club, family-friendly BARBÙ, The Portrait of Voyage Sky Bar and Phra Tamnak Viewpoint.
/en-gb/rooftops/cities/phuket/: Phuket rooftop bars for sunset: five venues mapped, from Baba Nest at Sri Panwa and Sizzle in Patong to Twilight Sky above Kata, Vanilla Sky at Kamala and The Surface at La Flora Resort.
/en-gb/rooftops/cocoa-xo/: Cocoa XO at Centara Grand at CentralWorld is a Bangkok rooftop dessert bar serving handmade chocolates and cognac cocktails with city views. Open daily 16:00–01:00; over-20s only.
/en-gb/rooftops/cru-champagne-bar/: CRU Champagne Bar on the 59th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld serves champagne and oysters above central Bangkok. Open daily 17:00–01:00 for over-20s; book through Reserve a Table.
/en-gb/rooftops/distil-lebua/: Distil on the 64th floor of lebua at State Tower in Silom pairs Bangkok night views with premium spirits, cocktails and cigars. Open 17:00–00:30; smart casual dress and over-20s only.
/en-gb/rooftops/doi-suthep-viewpoint/: Doi Suthep viewpoint sits within Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, where a terrace looks over Chiang Mai beside the golden chedi. Climb the 306 naga-lined steps or take the cable car up from the approach.
/en-gb/rooftops/flute-lebua/: Flûte is an open-air champagne bar on the 64th floor of lebua at State Tower, Bangkok, pairing Bollinger with oysters or caviar and jazz on nights other than Monday. Open 17:00–00:30.
/en-gb/rooftops/hongs-sky-bar/: HONG’s Sky Bar at InterContinental Chiang Mai The Mae Ping has an outdoor terrace facing Doi Suthep, with cocktails and Chinese sharing plates. Open 16:00–24:00; smart casual, may shut in rain.
/en-gb/rooftops/horizon-pattaya/: Horizon on the 34th floor of Hilton Pattaya is a rooftop restaurant with dinner and cocktails overlooking Pattaya Bay. Ideal for an anniversary at sunset; book through Hilton’s official dining page.
/en-gb/rooftops/iris-wild-iris/: IRIS & WILD IRIS on floors 29–30 of SO/ Bangkok overlook Lumphini Park, with Italian food, aperitifs and DJ music. Open Sunday to Thursday 17:00–00:00 and until 01:00 on Fridays and Saturdays.
/en-gb/rooftops/lebua-no3/: lebua No.3 on the 52nd floor of State Tower, Bangkok, is a contemporary gin and vodka bar serving caviar with city views. Open 17:00–00:30; smart casual dress and guests aged 20 and over.
/en-gb/rooftops/mahanakhon-skywalk/: Mahanakhon SkyWalk at King Power Mahanakhon has an indoor deck on floor 74 and an outdoor deck on 78 with a glass floor 310 m up. Open daily 10:00–24:00, last entry 23:00; book a timed slot.
/en-gb/rooftops/octave-rooftop/: Octave Rooftop at Bangkok Marriott Hotel Sukhumvit near Thong Lo serves food and drinks with views in every direction. Open daily 17:00 to 02:00, smart casual dress; reserve via the booking link.
/en-gb/rooftops/pastel-rooftop/: Pastel Rooftop on the 22nd floor of Aira Hotel Bangkok pairs Mediterranean dinner and cocktails with live music and city views. Open daily 17:00–01:00; check the events schedule for shows.
/en-gb/rooftops/phi-phi-viewpoint-2/: Phi Phi Viewpoint 2 is a hilltop lookout on Koh Phi Phi Don showing the sea and island village in one frame. Search for Viewpoint 2 by name, as the island has several, and allow time for the climb.
/en-gb/rooftops/phra-tamnak-viewpoint/: Phra Tamnak Viewpoint on the hill between South Pattaya and Jomtien looks over the curved bay and city. An outdoor lookout, not a bar, best at sunset; arrange transport back if leaving after dark.
/en-gb/rooftops/portrait-voyage-sky-bar/: The Portrait of Voyage Sky Bar on the 33rd floor of Grande Centre Point Voyage Pattaya is an open-air cocktail bar with sea views, open daily 11:30–24:00. Best for sunset drinks rather than a meal.
/en-gb/rooftops/red-sky-bar/: Red Sky Bar on the 56th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld serves cocktails and light bites with open views over Bangkok. Open daily 16:00–01:00; arrive before sunset after shopping.
/en-gb/rooftops/red-sky-restaurant/: Red Sky Restaurant on the 55th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld serves European dishes, steaks and seafood above Bangkok’s lights. Dinner daily 17:00–01:00; book via Reserve a Table.
/en-gb/rooftops/seen-riverside/: SEEN Restaurant & Bar on floors 26–27 of Avani+ Riverside Bangkok pairs dinner and drinks with Chao Phraya and city views, indoors or outdoors, with DJ music into the evening.
/en-gb/rooftops/sin-rooftop/: SIN Rooftop Bar on the 27th floor of Avani+ Riverside Bangkok is an open-air bar overlooking the Chao Phraya, open 17:00–01:00. It is separate from SEEN Restaurant & Bar in the same hotel.
/en-gb/rooftops/sirocco/: Sirocco on the 63rd floor of lebua at State Tower serves Mediterranean dinner beneath the golden dome, open 17:30–00:30. All ages welcome; book ahead, and note sportswear and flip-flops are banned.
/en-gb/rooftops/sizzle-rooftop/: Sizzle Rooftop at Avista Hideaway Phuket Patong – MGallery looks over the Andaman Sea and wooded hills. The bar opens 17:30–23:30 and the restaurant 18:00–23:00, with covered seats in rain.
/en-gb/rooftops/sky-bar/: Sky Bar by lebua on the 64th floor of State Tower overlooks the Chao Phraya beside the golden dome and serves the Hangovertini from The Hangover Part II. Walk-ins only, one drink minimum.
/en-gb/rooftops/sky-beach/: Sky Beach at The Standard, Bangkok Mahanakhon is an open-air bar at the top of King Power Mahanakhon with cocktails, American food and DJ music. Open daily 10:00–24:00; seating is first come.
/en-gb/rooftops/sky-on-20/: Sky on 20 on the 26th floor of Novotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 20 serves cocktails, pizza and crab mayonnaise bruschetta with city views. Open daily 17:00–01:00, with DJs on Friday and Saturday nights.
/en-gb/rooftops/skybar-summer-club/: Skybar Summer Club on the 27th floor of Siam@Siam Design Hotel Pattaya overlooks the Gulf of Thailand, with pools on two levels, cocktails and live DJs. Admission is for over-18s only.
/en-gb/rooftops/spectrum-lounge-bar/: Spectrum at Hyatt Regency Bangkok Sukhumvit offers dinner and live music on floor 29 and an open-air cocktail bar with DJs on floor 30. Open 17:30–01:00; smart casual, no sandals or sportswear.
/en-gb/rooftops/spire-rooftop/: Spire Rooftop Bar on the 39th floor of Dusit Thani Bangkok sits beneath the hotel’s golden spire, with Tropic City cocktails, bar food and DJs. Open daily 17:00–01:00; under-20s welcome until 19:00.
/en-gb/rooftops/star-silavadee/: STAR at Silavadee Pool Spa Resort is a Koh Samui rooftop above Lamai Bay with Western dishes, cocktails and four sunken tables in the infinity pool. Open 17:30–23:00; reserve on the venue page.
/en-gb/rooftops/surface-patong/: The Surface at La Flora Resort Patong is a rooftop serving cocktails and dinner with views over Patong Bay and the Andaman Sea, a relaxed way to end a beach day in Phuket at sunset.
/en-gb/rooftops/threesixty-rooftop/: ThreeSixty on the 31st floor of Millennium Hilton Bangkok offers drinks with broad views of the Chao Phraya River and skyline. Open 17:00–01:00; arrive around sunset to watch the boats and lights.
/en-gb/rooftops/tichuca-rooftop/: Tichuca on the 46th floor of the T-One Building in Bangkok is a jungle-styled rooftop with plants, cocktails and organic house from resident DJ collective Marichuca, made for a lively night out.
/en-gb/rooftops/twilight-sky/: Twilight Sky at The SIS Kata, an adults-only resort, is a restaurant and bar above Kata Beach and the Andaman Sea. Book by phone for a sunset dinner; a Thursday steak and live-music night is listed.
/en-gb/rooftops/vanilla-sky/: Vanilla Sky at Cape Sienna Phuket looks over Kamala Bay and Rayee Beach, serving the Smoky Cinnamon cocktail, draught beer and charcoal-grilled food. Open daily 17:00–24:00; book by email.
/en-gb/rooftops/yao-rooftop/: Yao Rooftop Bar at Bangkok Marriott Hotel The Surawongse has Chinese-inspired décor, dim sum and cocktails above central Bangkok and the old town. Open daily 17:00–01:00, casual dress.
/en-gb/transport/: Getting around Thailand: transport guides for Bangkok rail and stations, bus terminals, boats and piers, trains, domestic flights, taxis and ride hailing, motorbike taxis, tuk-tuks and songthaews.
/en-gb/beaches/cities/hua-hin/: Hua Hin beaches compared: the town beach beside this royal retreat town and Khao Takiab to the south. Combine a seaside walk with hill scenery, treating the temple and sand as separate stops.
/en-gb/beaches/cities/ko-samet/: Ko Samet beaches compared: white-sand Sai Kaew and the crescent bay of Ao Wong Duean. Arrange your boat from Ban Phe on the mainland and your arrival pier first, then the onward trip to the beach.
/en-gb/beaches/cities/samui/: Ko Samui beaches compared: Chaweng and Lamai on the east coast. Both have accommodation and restaurants, but their sand and seabed differ, so weigh scenery and swimming conditions together.
